That path is taken whenever the mover's x high byte differs from viewport_left_high (a flipped mover in a viewport that spans a 256-column boundary, or one off to the left), and the claim ignores it. The 2-byte shift is worse. Moving everything from &1BD7 to &3400 down 2 makes two hot branches newly cross a page, each +1 cycle when taken. It runs on every mover move with x_delta positive. (2) &3131 BPL cell, the back branch of sky mode's per-cell loop (src/sky_main.6502): next &3133, target &3101. After the shift they are &3131 and &30FF, which crosses. It runs per cell of every helicopter rectangle drawn. Those costs easily outweigh 1.9 cycles a pass. Only branches inside the moved region were checked. Indexed table reads on tables that move were not, which is another unverified source of +1s. cycles_per_execution_recounted is the worst path (-3, meaning 3 slower); the best path saves 2.
